questions.q: For Azure SQL Database (PaaS), what does a DBA need to do to make full, differential, and log backups happen?
options: Nothing — Microsoft runs them automatically on its own schedule, with no BACKUP DATABASE statement or scheduled job involved
Write and schedule a BACKUP DATABASE T-SQL job just like on-prem SQL Server
Manually trigger each backup type from the Azure Portal every day
Configure a SQL Server Agent job to run BACKUP DATABASE nightly
questions.explain: There is no BACKUP statement to write for Azure SQL Database — it isn't a different way to configure backups, there's simply nothing for the DBA to configure.

questions.q: Roughly how often does Azure SQL Database take transaction log backups automatically?
options: Every 5-10 minutes
Once a month
Only when the DBA manually requests it
Once per year
questions.explain: Log backups run far more frequently than full or differential backups — every 5-10 minutes — which keeps the point-in-time recovery window tight.

questions.q: What real responsibility does a DBA lose direct visibility into when using Azure SQL Database's automated backups, compared to on-prem SQL Server?
options: Verifying that backup jobs succeeded, investigating failures, and managing backup storage capacity
The ability to ever restore the database at all
Choosing which database to back up
Knowing what a full backup versus a differential backup is
questions.explain: This lesson states plainly that this is a genuine trade-off — a task on-prem DBAs are used to owning directly is removed entirely, not just automated in a way you still watch.

questions.q: Where are Azure SQL Database's automated backups stored, and what determines their redundancy?
options: Microsoft-managed Azure Storage, automatically inheriting the same redundancy option (LRS/ZRS/GRS) selected for the database itself
A separate Azure Storage account the DBA must create and configure manually
On the same disk as the database's data files
They are not stored anywhere — they exist only in memory
questions.explain: You don't pick a separate backup destination or redundancy setting; it inherits whatever redundancy tier the database itself uses.

questions.q: What does a DBA still control for Azure SQL Database's automated backups, even without controlling the backup schedule itself?
options: The retention window, an optional long-term retention (LTR) policy, and which redundancy tier the database uses
The exact time of day each backup type runs
Whether differential backups are taken at all
The file format Azure uses internally to store the backup
questions.explain: Retention and redundancy remain DBA-configurable settings — the mechanism and schedule of the backups themselves are the parts Microsoft owns.
